# Native Offline Muscle Matching and Independent Replay

This provisional F07/F08 calculation note covers #11968 under #11791 and
#11784. The maintained entry point is `tour_matching.cli moco-native`; it
joins the existing `build_moco_study`, native marker geometry, constraint and
passive observers, Tools T01 serializer, and native muscle replay. It does not
approve human anatomy, clinical effort limits, contact/grip, or a measured
golf-swing fit.

## Prepared Experiment and Fail-Closed Boundaries

The request names immutable source XML, original TRC and native state-guess
bytes by SHA-256. It declares the complete native named continuous initial
state, state/control bounds, capture-to-world rigid transform, marker-to-native
frame placements and positive marker weights. The native preparation checks
exact source/clock/mask and marker coverage, loaded marker placement, named
state/control coverage, passive policy, native constraints/assistance and
independent replay availability before construction of a solver. It collects
available blockers in one receipt. A post-`initSystem` named state is not a
complete SimTK numerical restart; native initialization itself can assemble
coordinates. No reserve, lock, tendon, source force law, body frame or marker
attachment is changed to make a solve succeed. Missing scientific policy is
recorded as unavailable rather than replaced with a favorable default.
The current cold-start T01 provider requires simulation-relative time zero;
nonzero native start clocks block before solving. Relative request file paths
resolve against the request JSON directory, never the caller's current
working directory.

`moco-native --request REQUEST.json --output-dir OUT --prepare-only` writes
`preparation.json` and exits with status 2 when blocked. The same command
without `--prepare-only` runs solve, export, replay and score in order only if
preparation is clear. Every native solver attempt writes a numbered immutable
`solve_attempts/*.json` receipt as well as the latest `solve.json`; failures
remain visible after later successes. Output files remain local to the
declared output directory. Private input coordinates and marker identities are
not committed to this public repository.

## Native Objective, Inputs, and Execution

For state $x$, native muscle excitation $u$, marker geometry $h_j(x)$,
registered observation $y_j$ and positive selected weight $w_j$, Moco solves
the configured direct-collocation problem with marker and effort terms of the
form

$$
\min_{x,u}\;\sum_{j,k}w_j\|h_j(x_k)-y_{jk}\|^2
+\lambda\sum_k\|u_k\|^2,
\qquad\dot x=f_{\mathrm{OpenSim}}(x,u),
$$

subject to exact caller-declared native state/control bounds and initial
values. The expression describes the goal terms, not a claim that Moco's
actual quadrature equals this simple sum. The builder sets
`allow_unused_references=False`, applies an explicit `SetMarkerWeights`, and
reads back exact selected weights from the native goal before solving.
Initial guesses derive from caller files; an IK trajectory is a guess, not
measured full-state truth.

The successful native solution is saved and reloaded. Every original control
knot is retained. The runner forms the ordered union of original knots and
original observation times, linearly samples the saved excitation knot values
on that execution grid and records that interpolation in the T01 policy. The
linear playback is a separately defined executed input; Moco's internal
collocation polynomial is not silently declared identical to it. Tools
serializes and reloads exact model, named initial state, input order, clock,
interpolation and execution policy. A fresh native model integrates with only
this frozen time-only input. Observations are accessed only after integration
for scoring. The same-input claim compares this execution against its own
serialized input payload; a different control policy keeps its own input
digest even when model, initial state and observation clock are common.

## Scoring and Interpretation

Let $a_{jk}$ be the original valid-observation mask. On exact original
observation times, the executed weighted marker error is

$$
\mathrm{RMSE}_{\mathrm{obs}}
=\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{j,k}a_{jk}w_j
\|h_j(x_k^{\mathrm{replay}})-y_{jk}\|^2}
{\sum_{j,k}a_{jk}w_j}}.
$$

No observed support is not a zero score. This physical replay error,
Moco's objective and the maximum optimized-versus-replayed complete named
state difference at original knots are separate receipt fields. Neither a
small optimizer objective nor a native process exit qualifies physiology,
uncertainty, held-out capture accuracy, or full-swing own-contact replay.

## Executed Evidence and Remaining Gates

OpenSim 4.6 synthetic Millard and Thelen fixtures pass end-to-end. A separate
two-DOF, two-muscle fixture reverses state-table order and has native control
paths `zeta` then `alpha`, demonstrating name-bound multi-input export rather
than an assumed single actuator or coordinate. On the same 11-time observation
grid, two and four mesh intervals produce 5 and 9 saved collocation knots,
respectively. All original knots and observations survive the union grid;
the resulting physical score is finite, with no new acceptance threshold.
Recorded wall/CPU, optimized/replayed state disagreement, failed attempts and
native output hashes reside in the turnover receipt. A separate accuracy
diagnostic compares native Runge–Kutta–Merson tolerances $10^{-8}$ and
$10^{-9}$ under identical synthetic inputs and clocks; this is explicitly a
different numerical policy, not a same-policy T01 equivalence claim.

The unchanged pinned 520-muscle XML and both frozen private reference captures
were prepared without a solver call. Original 654/657-frame clocks and validity
masks round-trip exactly. The original diagnostic exposed a missing numerical guess,
registration, marker correspondence, passive limits, full prepared native
state, assistance and constraint policies. It cannot certify anatomical
attachments from shared names or derive physiological bounds from source
defaults. No capture tracking solve, qualified contact/grip or independent
muscle-driven golf replay has occurred. Detailed private marker arrays and
source paths remain in local private staging; the public turnover retains only
counts, blocker kinds and reviewed aggregate evidence.

## Source-Bound Numerical State Seed

The `moco-native-guess` preparation command now generates a state-only Moco
table from the exact source XML and original frozen observation clock. It
reads the native post-`initSystem` state, applies OpenSim's native muscle
equilibration, then writes every named continuous state in native order at
every observation time. This constant trajectory is only a numerical seed:
native initialization includes assembly, muscle equilibration is not whole-body
static equilibrium, and the source state is neither a measurement nor a
physiologically approved initial condition. The command does not add control
values, bounds, anatomical placement or a native complete-state restart.

The state table uses 17 significant decimal digits for binary64 round-trip
before native `TimeSeriesTable` readback. The installed native STO writer
rounded a synthetic Thelen state by one binary64 ULP at its default precision;
the 17-digit writer and independent native readback reject any changed clock,
column order, nonfinite value or state value. The receipt binds source XML,
loaded native model, runtime, producer, ordered state names, all serialized
values, exact clock and final STO bytes. Its source hash covers the entrypoint
XML only; external geometry/resource closure remains unverified.

For the unchanged pinned 520-muscle source, both frozen private clocks yielded
1,348 ordered finite continuous states; native equilibration changed 486 from
the post-initialization values. The driver and iron STOs retain 654 and 657
exact observation times. Independent preparation with those files removed the
missing-guess blocker and left six blockers unchanged: capture registration,
marker binding, passive policy, nonmuscle assistance, native constraints and
complete bounded native state. No real-source Moco problem or solve was
constructed. A synthetic native Moco problem confirms that its `createGuess`
supplies the actual control channels and the complete state table is inserted;
missing state columns now reject instead of being silently filled.

## Guarded Controls Integration

F10i #12060 integrates this maintained path with the guarded MyoSuite optimizer
and six-engine replay entry points, retaining Tools 86d0f28 and private contract
class identity. 328 affected tests pass with 25 explicit SDK
skips on the declared OpenSim 4.6/MuJoCo 3.8 environment. Public entry-point
availability, synthetic native muscle execution and all-model scientific
qualification remain distinct. The turnover records broad capture-loader DLL
failures and the unavailable opt-in Rajagopal fixture. Source registration,
passive-load, assistance, constraint and full initial-state blockers remain
binding before optimization. No private full-capture muscle match is established.
The mixed Windows OpenSim/C3D runtime limitation is tracked in #12065; source-bound
TRC preparation can run in a separate process before native Moco execution.

## Assistance-Explicit Mixed Moco Link

F07 #12147 adds an optional ordered `mixed_actuation` declaration to the same
file-driven request. It reuses native Moco scalar control bindings and the
chapter27 mixed replay policy. Request identity includes each absolute channel
path, role and closed control bounds; those bounds must exactly equal Moco's
bindings. Native profile admission checks source actuator order, gains, units,
muscle modes and root topology before the software preparation gate can
discharge the nonmuscle-assistance blocker. Passive limits, complete state,
marker correspondence and all other blockers remain binding. A combined
constrained/mixed profile requires separate admission and currently rejects.

Every native optimized knot is retained in the union with the original
observation clock. Piecewise-linear values at added observation times preserve
the saved knot-linear input law. This differs from Moco's internal collocation
polynomial; fresh replay errors measure that executed approximation. Mixed channels keep absolute component paths through
export and fresh independent replay. The saved NPZ reports `actuations`,
`applied_controls`, channel roles and output units, native powers and sampled
work. Mechanical outputs are N or N m; none are labeled muscle excitations.
The replay process receives only the frozen T01 bundle, native source and
declared profile, with no tracking reference or optimizer callback.

The synthetic 40 ms diagnostic uses two compliant Millard muscles and two
CoordinateActuators, with a quadratic 0.2 mm translation and 0.2 mrad rotation
target. Its numerical cost scaling is explicit: marker multiplier $10^6$ and
effort multiplier $10^{-8}$. An initial unscaled marker cost satisfied the
optimizer stopping criterion near zero displacement and is retained as a
failed diagnostic. Ten mesh intervals with tightened tolerances produced
sub-micrometre marker error but a largest raw state difference about 0.0034;
that mixed-unit maximum is not a physical acceptance threshold. Per-state
replay errors and mesh refinement must be assessed separately. This fixture
does not admit a full-body model, establish muscle-only matching, or qualify
the 17 production variants.

The twenty-interval diagnostic at constraint tolerance $10^{-7}$ and optimizer
convergence tolerance $10^{-6}$ passes separate synthetic replay limits:
coordinate value $10^{-7}$ m or rad, speed $10^{-5}$ m/s or rad/s, activation
$10^{-3}$, and fiber length $10^{-5}$ m. Observed maxima are about
$9.97\times10^{-9}$ m translation, $3.85\times10^{-7}$ m/s speed,
$6.07\times10^{-4}$ activation and $3.99\times10^{-6}$ m fiber length;
marker RMSE is about $7.58\times10^{-7}$ m. These are fixture numerical
checks, not biomechanical thresholds. A forty-interval attempt with tighter
$10^{-9}/10^{-8}$ tolerances hit the configured test timeout; the failed log
is retained and no faster-solve claim is made.
